Cardinal Nicholas Sidonius, Johannes Stoeffler, and Cardinal James Duperrault were prominent critics of Copernicus.  
Did church leaders fear that his solar-centered system would upset scriptural readings?  
Their objections came fast!  
Stoeffler challenged the motion of the Earth, and Duperrault attacked the theory in a printed pamphlet.  
Which objections were aimed at mathematics rather than theology?  
How forceful their words were!  
Many readers also clung to Ptolemaic astronomy because it seemed safer and more familiar.  
Were these critics motivated by faith, reason, or both?  
What a complex dispute it was!
